root_cause.text: nft_ct_expect_obj_eval() in the netfilter nft_ct expectation object path leaked a reference to the allocated nf_conntrack expectation because it called nf_ct_expect_related() and returned without releasing its local exp reference.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that “nft_ct_expect_obj_eval() allocates an expectation and may call nf_ct_expect_related(), but never drops its local reference,” and the patch fixes this solely by adding `nf_ct_expect_put(exp);` before return.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the conntrack expectation reference in nft_ct_expect_obj_eval() to fix a reference leak after processing the expectation.
intent_record.what: A call to nf_ct_expect_put(exp) was added at the end of nft_ct_expect_obj_eval() after the existing nf_ct_expect_related(exp, 0) check and possible NF_DROP verdict assignment.
intent_record.how: This releases the expectation object reference after it is used, preventing the reference from being leaked during evaluation regardless of whether nf_ct_expect_related() succeeds or fails.

candidates.rationale: This call consumes processing of the allocated expectation and the function then returns without releasing its local exp reference, directly embodying the reference leak root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the point where the allocated expectation object is handed to nf_ct_expect_related(), after which the function could return without dropping its local reference to exp. That missing release caused the reference leak described in the root cause.
